title: Find Corporate Domains
description:
An enterprise tier is restricted to employees of three partner companies, identified by their email domain: `acme.com`, `globex.com`, and `initech.com`.

Write a query to return the `id`, `name`, and `email` of every customer whose email belongs to one of these three domains exactly. Note that `dave@fakeacme.com` does **not** qualify — the domain must match precisely after the `@`.

Return the result in any order.
hint: The `$` must be anchored at the end, and `|` alternation provides the choices: `@(acme|globex|initech)\.com$`. Escape the dot before 'com' as `\.` so it is a literal dot.
outputExplanation:
- `bob@acme.com` — domain is exactly `acme.com`. Returned. ✓
- `carol@globex.com` — domain is exactly `globex.com`. Returned. ✓
- `dave@fakeacme.com` — domain is `fakeacme.com`, not `acme.com`. Not returned. ✗
- `alice@acme.co` — TLD is `.co`, not `.com`. Not returned. ✗
- `eve@initech.com` — domain is exactly `initech.com`. Returned. ✓
- `fred@acme.com.mx` — `.mx` appended after `.com`; the end anchor rejects it. Not returned. ✗

Rows 1, 2, and 5 are returned.
